name: quiet-scrapbook
title: Quiet archival scrapbook
nearest: scrapbook (v1 wave; the loud sibling: foxed parchment, ransom titles, copperplate everywhere)

recipe.mark: flat pieces of coloured stock with a fine torn deckle; typewriter strikes (one weight, each strike its own ink density); thin steady technical-pen diagrams; ONE small vintage engraving as ornament; a red pen and a blue pencil used once or twice each
recipe.edge: torn but tidy: an even fine deckle, never ragged; every piece throws the same soft shadow down-right (lamp upper left); ink lines clean and unhatched outside the engraving
recipe.order: page; cards laid down big first; coloured label chips; the diagram inked on its card; typed labels; the engraving; red and blue annotations last
recipe.paper: a pale warm sheet (#efe7d3), barely aged: soft mottle, slight darkening toward the edges; no foxing, tape or pegs
recipe.layout rule: mostly empty page; pieces are islands with air round them; one diagram card is the focal piece

profile.summary: high key (mean L 0.86), contrast 0.23, 5 colours over 2%, low chroma 0.03 with one vermilion accent, line presence 1.8% (mostly type), pooled rims 0.42 (card shadows), no lattice. The statistical nearest was wren: the empty page dominates the numbers, which is why the plate was picked by eye

provenance.reference: refs/ritwika-explainer/frames/f_10.png (1280x720), frame 10 of Ritwika's explainer film
provenance.copied: nothing: its subject (a frozen-LLM encoder), diagram (bars in a box, a vector), quote card, padlock engraving, asterisk and progress dots are not used; the proof subject (why sourdough rises) and its layout are new

knownGaps: the typewriter is capitals only (drafting.ts has no lowercase); the reference types lowercase serif
no brush-script hand yet (lettering.ts spells one authored word)
